en.overview:
Flexi Day is a shared calendar for time off and attendance. People belong to an organization,
which holds one or more groups. Each group has its own working days, holiday country, members and
approvers.

## What people do in Flexi Day

- **Time off.** Members send requests for vacation and other absences on the Requests
  page. Approvers in the group approve or reject them. Quotas track how many days each person has
  in a year.
- **The calendar.** The Dashboard shows who is away. The Report page sums up
  time off for a group or a person, with an Excel export.
- **Calendar sync.** Time off can appear in Google or Microsoft calendars through a feed or a
  direct sync.
- **Attendance.** Where the organization turns it on, people clock in and out, and group admins
  and organization administrators see worked time on Team attendance.
- **Directory.** On Enterprise, the people directory keeps employments and profiles.
- **Group events and birthdays** show on the calendar beside time off.

## Roles

The owner pays for the organization and can name org admins. Each group has a manager, approvers
and members. What a person can see and change depends on these roles.

## Plans

Organizations start on the Free plan. Pro costs €8 a month and Enterprise
€16 a month, excluding VAT. The owner manages the plan on the
Billing page.

## AI features

The Assistant is a chat in the web app on Enterprise. AI connections let apps such as Claude or
ChatGPT work with Flexi Day on Pro and Enterprise. The owner turns each of them on.

articles.title: Change your settings
articles.summary: Email notifications, the dashboard calendar layout, language and theme, and where the other account settings live.
articles.body:
Open Settings from the sidebar or from the user menu in the top bar. These settings belong
to your account, so they apply in every organization you work in.

## Email notifications

"Email notifications" controls the emails Flexi Day sends about requests: approval
requests for approvers, decisions on your requests, cancellations, and comments. Turn it off and
these updates reach you only in the app, in the bell in the top bar, and on your iPhone if you use
the app. Account emails, such as confirming your address or resetting your password, always send. See
[Notifications and emails](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/notifications/).

## The dashboard calendar

The "Dashboard calendar" card sets how the Dashboard calendar opens:

- **Layout.** "Lanes" puts names on the calendar.
  "Stripes" keeps the month compact; pick a day to see who is away. The iPhone
  app uses the same choice.
- **Whose time off to show.** "Only me" or "My group".
  With the group, choose which one. Only groups whose time off you may view are listed; a group
  admin can give you view access.

You can still switch between yourself and a group for one visit on the dashboard itself.

## Language and theme

Switch between English and Czech with the language button in the top bar; the choice is saved with
your account. The theme button picks light, dark, or your system's setting.

## Your name and email address

Your name and email address are the ones you signed up with. The app has no field to change them
yet.

## Other settings on this page

- **Birthday**: whether your groups see your birthday on their calendar. See
  [Add your birthday and share it](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/birthdays/).
- **Sign-in methods**, **Change password** and
  **Two-factor authentication**: see [Sign in to Flexi Day](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/sign-in/).
- **AI connections**: the AI apps you connected, with Disconnect. See
  [Connect an AI app to Flexi Day](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/ai-connections/).
- **Your data** and **Delete account**: see
  [Download your data or delete your account](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/delete-your-account/).

articles.title: Limits on AI connections
articles.summary: The daily AI connection limit, the member daily limit and the limits for each app, and what an AI app hears when it reaches one.
articles.body:
AI connections have limits, so that one app or one person can't use up what the whole organization
shares. Only the app's tool calls count. Connecting, listing what the app can do and checking the
connection don't.

## Daily limits

- **Daily AI connection limit**: the calls all of an organization's AI connections may make in one
  day, together. 5,000 on Pro, 20,000 on Enterprise and Custom.
- **Member daily limit**: 1,000 per person in each organization, so one app stuck in a loop can't
  use the whole organization's day.

Both reset at midnight UTC. The owner sees both numbers when turning AI connections on in the AI
card on the Organization page.

## Limits for each app

Each app a person connected may make 300 tool calls in 5 minutes and 30 changes an hour. A change
is creating or cancelling a request, or clocking in or out; each can send emails, which is why
changes have a lower limit. A person's second app has limits of its own.

## When a limit is reached

The app gets a message in your app language saying which limit it reached and when it resets, so
it can tell you. Until then its calls are refused. Flexi Day itself keeps working, and so do your
other apps, unless the organization reached its daily AI connection limit, which every app there
shares. Nobody gets an email or a notification.

articles.title: Connect an AI app to Flexi Day
articles.summary: Let an AI app such as Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor read your Flexi Day data and make changes for you.
headings: What a connected app can do
articles.body:
AI connections let an AI app you already use, such as Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor, work with your
Flexi Day data. The app acts as you, in one organization, with the same permissions you have in the
app.

## Before you start

AI connections work on every paid plan: Pro, Enterprise and Custom. The owner chooses one of three
settings for "AI connections" in the AI card on the
Organization page:

- **Off**, the default: no app can connect.
- **Read only**: apps can read what you can see.
- **Read and write**: apps can also make changes to your own
  records.

## Turning AI connections on

Only the owner can change the setting. Org admins see it but can't change it, and on the Free plan
it stays off. Before AI connections turn on, the owner reads what the apps can do and what leaves
Flexi Day: what an app reads goes to the company behind that app, under the member's own agreement
with them. Personal accounts of AI apps may keep what they read or train on it, so your
organization's own policy decides which apps people may use.

The owner picks the level to start with under "Start with". The
first time an AI feature is turned on, the owner accepts the AI features agreement for the
organization, and Flexi Day records who accepted, when, and which version. If the Assistant already
accepted the current version, AI connections don't ask again.

"Tell members" is ticked by default and sends everyone in the organization a
notice in the app and on their phone. While AI connections are on, the owner can copy the same text
from the AI card with "Copy the members' notice".

Going from Read only to
Read and write needs no new acceptance. Lowering to
Read only or turning AI connections off asks the owner to confirm
first and names the apps and people it disconnects. Every change is recorded with who made it and
when.

## Connect an app

1. Open Settings and find the "AI connections" card.
2. Under "Connect an AI app", copy the server address,
   `https://api.flexi-day.com/mcp`.
3. In your AI app, add a custom connector with that address.
4. The app opens a Flexi Day page that names it. Sign in as usual. If you use two-factor
   authentication, Flexi Day asks for your code. Nothing is shared until you allow it.
5. Pick the organization the app should work in. Each one shows the access it allows.
   Organizations whose owner hasn't turned on AI connections, or that are on the Free plan, are
   listed with the reason. If none allows it, go back to the app.
6. Check the consent page and choose "Allow".

Each connection covers one organization, and you pick it every time you connect. Connect again to
add another.

### The consent page

- When Flexi Day could check the app's address, the page says "Address checked" with it.
  Otherwise it says "Name not verified": the name is the app's own claim.
- When the app is a program on your computer, such as Claude Code or Cursor, a warning asks you to
  allow it only if you started connecting from it just now.
- "See what you can see" is always part of the connection. "Make changes for you"
  is ticked; untick it to connect read only. On a Read only organization it isn't offered.

## What a connected app can do

It can read whatever you can see in Flexi Day and look things up in the help. With Read and write
it can also create a request, cancel your own request, and clock you in or out, only for you.
Flexi Day makes the change at once, under the same rules as in the app. It can't approve or
reject requests (do that in Flexi Day, or ask [the Assistant](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/assistant/)), and it can't change roles, billing or
settings.

A change the app makes reads "through an AI app" in the request's history or in the
attendance history. When it opens a Sensitive section of someone's profile, the organization's Read
log shows the read the same way.

## Limits

Each organization has a daily AI connection limit, each person a member daily limit, and each app
limits of its own. [Limits on AI connections](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/ai-connection-limits/) has the numbers and what
the app hears when it reaches one.

## Your connections and Disconnect

The "AI connections" card in Settings lists each app you
connected: its address, or "name not verified" when Flexi Day couldn't
check it, the organization, its access, and when it was last used. Last use updates at least once an hour while the app is in use.

To end one, choose "Disconnect" next to the app and confirm. The
app stops at its next call. To use it again, connect it again.

### What else disconnects apps

- Resetting your password disconnects every app you connected, in every organization.
- Changing your password in Settings does the same, because it also signs you out
  everywhere else.
- Deleting your account disconnects them all.
- The owner turning AI connections off disconnects every app in the organization. Lowering it to
  Read only disconnects the apps that have write access; connect
  again to get read access.
- Owners and org admins see each person's apps on the AI usage page and can revoke them there.

Signing out, turning on two-factor authentication and a lapsed plan keep your connections. While the plan is lapsed, the app's calls are refused.

articles.title: The AI usage page
articles.summary: What owners and org admins see on the AI usage page, from the Assistant's spend to each person's AI apps, and how to revoke an app.
articles.body:
The AI usage page shows what the Assistant and your members' AI apps use in one
organization. Only the owner and org admins see it. Open it from AI usage under
Organization in the sidebar, from "See AI usage" on the AI
card of the Organization page, or from "See usage" when the
Assistant has paused. If you administer more than one organization, pick one at the top.

It shows what each person used and how many of their messages were refused, never what anyone
wrote.

## Assistant this week

How much of the organization's Weekly limit is used, in dollars and as a percentage, and when it
resets, in your own time zone. Answers still being written count, so the figure can drop a little
once they finish. Bars show the last eight weeks beside this one, with the weeks that reached the
limit in red. Once the limit is reached, the card says when, and that the Assistant is paused for
everyone until the reset. See [Weekly limit and Usage](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/assistant-weekly-limit/).

## AI connections today

The tool calls all AI apps made today against the daily AI connection limit, when the count resets,
and bars for the last 14 days with the days that reached the limit in red. See
[Limits on AI connections](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/ai-connection-limits/).

## People

One row per person who used the Assistant this week, had a message refused, made a call today or
has an AI app connected:

- **Assistant this week**: what their Assistant answers cost this week.
- **Refused**: messages the Assistant refused as off topic or unsafe this
  week. From 3 the number turns amber.
- **AI calls today**: their AI apps' calls today, marked once they reach the
  member daily limit.
- **Connected apps**: the apps they connected in this organization.

Usage of an account that was deleted and erased shows as "Deleted account",
with no name, so the totals stay right. On a phone each person is a card.

## Revoke an app

Open a person to see their apps, with the access each has, when it was connected and when it was
last used. Press Revoke, then Revoke again to confirm.
The app stops at its next call. The person can connect it again while AI connections are on, and
they can disconnect their own apps in Settings. See [AI connections](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/ai-connections/).

## Past weeks

Every earlier week with Assistant use, newest first, with the date the limit was reached if it was.
Open a week to see who used how much. Per-person usage is kept for 180 days; older weeks show only
the organization's total.

If both the Assistant and AI connections are off, the page says so and links to the organization
settings.

articles.title: Allowances and how many days you have left
articles.summary: How yearly allowances work per group and type, where to see what's left, and how admins set them.
articles.body:
An allowance is the number of days a person may book of one type in one year, in one group. Three
types have one: Vacation,
Home Office, and Sick day where
the Sick day benefit is on. The numbers are your organization's own; group admins set them.

## See what you have left

"My balance" on the Dashboard shows, for each type with an allowance,
the days left out of the total for this year, summed over your groups. Days waiting for approval are
noted beside it. The group's Quotas tab shows each member's allowance for a
year, if you have the View permission there.

## How booking uses it

- Each group has its own allowances. Time off booked in a group draws on that group's.
- A day counts against the year it falls in. A half day counts 0.5.
- A new request is refused if your approved and pending days plus the new ones would pass the
  allowance. Cancelling a request gives its days back.
- Unused Vacation days carry over into the next year; see
  [Year-end carry-over](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/year-rollover/).

If a request is refused for that reason, ask a group admin to raise your allowance.

## Set a member's allowance

Group admins, the manager and organization administrators can do this.

1. Open the group from Groups and go to Quotas.
2. Pick the year with the arrows.
3. Press "Edit" next to the member, change the numbers and save.

A member with no allowance saved for a year shows the group default, marked
"(default)". Saving writes their own number. Every change is recorded, with who made
it, under "Changes by admins" on the member's page in the Report.

The days carried over from last year are set in "Edit quota" on that same page,
which suggests the unused days from the year before.

## Group defaults

Under "Group defaults" on the Quotas tab, admins set the
allowances new members start with. Press "Save defaults" to keep them. Defaults
apply to members who have no allowance for a year yet; existing allowances don't change.

## External workers

External workers have no allowance and can book only types without one.

articles.title: Approve or decline time off requests
articles.summary: Where approvers find waiting requests, how to approve or decline with a reason, and who may decide.
articles.body:
Requests in a group are decided by its approvers: members with the Approver permission, and the
group's manager. You get an email and a notice in the app when a request waits for you.

## Find waiting requests

- **Dashboard:** the "Pending approvals" card lists what waits on you, with
  "Approve" and "Decline" buttons.
- **Requests:** pick the group and the months, then filter by
  "Pending". Each row is one whole request, with
  "Approve" and "Reject" buttons.
- **The calendar:** click a request to open its details.

## Decide with a reason

Open the request details to see the dates, the type, the note, the files and the history. Type a
comment or reason in the box, then press "Approve" or
"Decline". The comment appears in the request's history and the member is
notified of the decision.

A decision covers the whole request, every day of it. A declined request is final; the member books
again if needed. An approved request can still be cancelled later, by the member or by you.

To ask a question without deciding, write it and press "Comment". The member is
notified, and their reply notifies the approvers.

## Who may decide

- Members with the Approver permission and the group's manager.
- Not organization administrators: they manage groups but decide on nobody's leave. To approve, they
  need the Approver permission inside the group.
- Not on records mirrored in from another group. They are decided in the group they were booked in.

You can decide your own request only if you hold the Approver permission in that group. Otherwise
another approver decides it.

## Allowances when approving

Approving checks the member's allowance for that type and year, counting only days already approved.
A request that would take them past it can't be approved; a group admin can raise the allowance
first. See [Allowances](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/allowances/).

articles.title: Confirm changes the Assistant prepares
articles.summary: How the Assistant's confirmation cards work, for your own changes and for approving or rejecting requests, and what happens when you confirm one, decline it or move on.
headings: A note written by someone else
articles.body:
Ask the Assistant to book time off, cancel one of your own requests, or clock you in or out, and it
prepares the change as a card in the chat. Approvers can also approve or reject requests this way.
Nothing changes until you confirm the card.

## What a card shows

The card asks a question, such as "Send this request?", and lists the
details Flexi Day worked out with the same rules the app uses: the type, the dates, the working
days, your balance before and after, and the group. A note or reason you asked for appears word for
word, with a line saying whose words they are. The details come from Flexi Day, never from the
Assistant's own wording. Every card says "Marked as made through the Assistant".

If the rules don't allow the change, for example because your balance is too low, you get no card.
The Assistant tells you why instead.

## Confirm or leave it

- "Send request", "Cancel request",
  "Clock in" or "Clock out" makes the
  change. Flexi Day checks the rules again at that moment. The card shrinks to one line with the
  result and "Open", which opens your requests or your attendance.
- "Not now", or "Keep it" on a cancellation, leaves
  everything as it was.
- If the change fails when you confirm, for example because the day was booked in the meantime, the
  card shows the reason in red and stays open. "Try again" tries once more.
- Sending a new message instead marks any card still waiting as not taken. It can't be confirmed
  afterwards; ask again for a fresh card.

When the Assistant prepares two changes at once, each gets its own card and you decide them one by
one. It carries on writing once you have decided them all.

A change made this way reads "through the Assistant" in the request's history or in the
attendance history of that day. Approvers are notified as for a request made in the app.

## Approve or reject a request

If you approve time off, ask "What's waiting for my approval?" and the Assistant lists the requests
waiting for you. Ask it to approve or reject one and you get a card with the requester, the type, the
dates, the working days, their balance before and after, the group, and the request's own note word
for word with who wrote it. The Assistant never recommends approving or rejecting; the decision is
yours.

- "Approve" approves every day of the request still waiting.
- "Reject" rejects them. The card has a field for a reason the
  requester reads; leave it empty to reject without one.

The requester is notified as when you decide in the app, and the request's history reads
"through the Assistant". The same rules apply as in the app: you decide only in groups
where you approve, and an approval must fit the requester's allowance. Approving and rejecting work
only in the Assistant, not in AI apps you connect.

## A note written by someone else

Before preparing a change, the Assistant may read text other people wrote, such as the note on a
colleague's time off or a group event's title. When it did, the card names who wrote it and asks you
to check that this is what you asked for. Someone could write a note meant to steer the Assistant,
so make sure the card matches what you asked for before you confirm.

## At the Weekly limit

A card already shown stays confirmable when your organization reaches its Weekly limit. Confirming
makes the change, but the Assistant replies to it only after the limit resets, with your next
message. See [Weekly limit and Usage](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/assistant-weekly-limit/).

articles.title: Weekly limit and Usage
articles.summary: How the Assistant's Usage counts against your organization's Weekly limit, and what happens near and at the limit.
articles.body:
Usage is what the Assistant's answers cost your organization: the AI provider's list price for
each step of an answer, answers still being written included. Each organization has a Weekly limit
on Usage, shared by everyone in it. It resets every Monday at 00:00 UTC, shown in your own time
zone.

## Near the limit

From 80% of the limit, a bar under the message box shows how much is used and when it resets.
Members see the percentage; owners and org admins also see the amounts.

## When the limit is reached

The Assistant pauses for the whole organization until the reset, and the message box says until
when. Your chats stay readable. An answer that reaches the limit halfway keeps what it wrote and
ends with a line saying it stopped. Owners and org admins get "See usage",
which opens the [AI usage](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/ai-usage/) page with the organization's usage, person by
person.

## Assistant unavailable

"The Assistant is unavailable right now. Try again later." means the AI provider itself can't answer. It isn't your
organization's limit, and nothing counts against it.

articles.title: What the Assistant can do
articles.summary: Ask the Assistant about Flexi Day in plain language, and let it prepare changes you confirm.
articles.body:
The Assistant is a chat in the Flexi Day web app. Ask it a question in English or Czech and it
answers from the help articles and from the data you can already see in the app. It sees exactly
what you can see, nothing more.

## Who can use it

The Assistant comes with the Enterprise plan. It is off until the owner turns it on in the AI card
on the Organization page. Once it is on, every member finds an "Assistant"
button in the top bar on every page. The iPhone app doesn't have it.

Until then, members don't see the button. On a plan without Enterprise only the owner sees it, and
it explains what Enterprise adds. On Enterprise with the Assistant off, the owner and org admins see
it, with a link to the organization settings.

## Using the panel

The button opens a panel on the right of the page, so you can keep working beside it. On a phone it
fills the screen. A new chat suggests a few questions to start with. If more than one of your
organizations has the Assistant, pick the organization before your first message: a chat stays in
the one it starts in.

You see each step the Assistant takes, such as checking your balance, above its answer. While an
answer is being written you can't send another message. If the connection drops, the panel says the
answer is still being written and picks it up again.

"Your chats" lists your chats under Today,
This week and Earlier. You can delete a chat there;
it can't be brought back. "New chat" starts a fresh one.

## Turning it on and off

Only the owner can turn the Assistant on or off, with the switch in the AI card on the
Organization page. Org admins see the switch but can't change it. Before it turns on, the
owner reads what the Assistant does and what leaves Flexi Day. The first time, they accept the AI
features agreement for the organization, and Flexi Day records who accepted, when, and which
version.

"Tell members" is ticked by default and sends everyone in the organization a
notice in the app and on their phone. The owner can copy the same text from the AI card with
"Copy the members' notice", for example into your own policy.

When a new version of the agreement comes out, the owner sees a banner on every page until they
accept it. The Assistant keeps working meanwhile. Turning the Assistant off takes it away from
members at once; their chats stay readable until they are 180 days old.

## What you can ask

- How-to questions, such as how to book half a day or how to clock in. Answers from the help end
  with "From the help:" links to the articles they came from.
- Questions about your own data and what you are allowed to see: how many days you have left, who
  is away next week, whether a request was approved, how much you worked this week.
- For approvers, the details of a request waiting for a decision.

Small talk, "what can you do" and questions about plans and pricing are fine too.

## What it won't answer

The Assistant answers Flexi Day questions only. Every message is checked before the Assistant sees
it. A message about anything else, or one that tries to change the Assistant's rules, isn't sent:
it stays in the chat marked "Not sent to the Assistant", followed by a short fixed reply
saying what the Assistant helps with. Owners and org admins see how many of each person's messages
were refused this week, never what anyone wrote.

If the check itself fails, nothing is sent and "Try again" sends the message
again, as "Send again" does after a dropped connection.

- It doesn't give legal advice. Ask your HR team or your employer.
- It doesn't write emails or letters. It offers to create the request with a short note instead.
- It never recommends approving or rejecting someone's request. It shows the facts, and the approver
  decides.
- People you can't see in Flexi Day don't appear in its answers.
- A note or name someone wrote that reads like instructions to the Assistant is hidden from it.
- Its answers link only to Flexi Day pages and help articles. Other links show as plain text, and
  images never show.

## Changes you confirm

The Assistant can prepare a change, such as a request or a clock-in, as a card with the exact
details. Nothing changes until you confirm the card.
[Confirm changes the Assistant prepares](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/assistant-changes/) explains the cards.

## Weekly limit

Each organization has a Weekly limit on the Assistant's Usage, shared by everyone in it. It resets
every Monday at 00:00 UTC. The "Weekly limit and Usage" article explains what counts and what you
see as the limit nears.

## Chats

Each chat belongs to one organization. A chat closes when it gets too long or after 30 days without
a message; you can still read it, and you start a new chat to carry on. Chats are deleted 180 days
after their last message, and you can delete one yourself at any time. When you leave an
organization, your chats in it are deleted.

The Assistant runs on Anthropic's Claude models. The AI features agreement the owner accepts
explains where chats are stored and for how long.

articles.title: Attach files to a request
articles.summary: Add a doctor's note or another image or PDF to a request, who can see it, and how long it is kept.
headings: On the Free plan or after a lapse
articles.body:
You can attach files to a request, such as a doctor's note. Attachments need a paid plan.

## Add files

- **When you create the request:** after you press "Submit Request", the form stays open
  with "Add files". Click it or drop files on it.
- **Later:** open the request from the calendar or the Requests page. The request details
  have the same "Attachments" section.

Each request holds up to five files. Each file can be PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC or PDF, up to 10 MB.

Every file is checked after upload. Images are converted to JPEG, shrunk to at most 2048 pixels on
the long side, and stripped of hidden metadata such as location. A file is rejected when its contents
don't match its type, an image can't be read, or a PDF contains scripts or a password. The reason
shows next to the file; replace it with another one.

## Who sees attachments

You, the approvers of the request's group and its admins, including organization administrators.
Teammates never see them.

You can open, preview and download a file from the request details.

## Remove a file

Whoever uploaded a file can delete it, and so can the group's admins. The file is removed for
everyone, and the request history keeps a note that it was there and who removed it.

## How long files are kept

Files are deleted automatically:

- 12 months after the request's last day;
- as soon as every day of the request is cancelled or rejected.

You can't attach new files after either point.

## On the Free plan or after a lapse

Without a paid plan, the "Attachments" section says attachments need one. Files already
attached stay available.

articles.title: Forgotten clock-outs and auto-closed sessions
articles.summary: What happens when a session or break runs past the organization's ceiling, how the auto-closed flag appears, and how to set the real time.
articles.body:
A ceiling is the longest a session or a break may run. When someone forgets to clock out or to end
a break, Flexi Day closes it at the ceiling and flags it, so a forgotten clock-out doesn't count as
a day that never ends.

## The two ceilings

| Ceiling                                              | Default  | Range                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------- |
| "Close a session after" | 16 hours | 1 to 24 hours          |
| "Close a break after"   | 2 hours  | 15 minutes to 24 hours |

Organization administrators change them in the "Attendance" card on the
Organization page.

## What happens

A nightly run closes a session that passed its ceiling at the moment the ceiling was reached: a
session started at 08:00 with a 16-hour ceiling ends at midnight. A break that ran past its own ceiling
ends there too, and never after its session.

You get one notice in the app, linking to the day. On My attendance the day shows a
"Auto-closed" mark and a message saying when it was closed. It does not stop you
from clocking in again.

A session still running from an earlier day, not yet closed by the nightly run, shows as
"Still open". Clock out to close it.

## Set the real time

1. Open the flagged day on My attendance and press "Correct".
2. Change the clock-out to the time you actually left, or a break's end to when you came back.
3. Save.

Correcting the clock-out clears the flag. You can do this yourself only inside your organization's
self-service window; otherwise ask a group admin or an organization admin. See
[Correct your attendance](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/attendance-corrections/).

## For admins

Auto-closed sessions show on Team attendance with their own mark, so you can see who still
has to set a real time. Correcting the clock-out yourself clears the flag the same way.

articles.title: Correct your attendance or add a session you forgot
articles.summary: How to fix a clock-in or clock-out time, add a missed session or break, and how far back the organization's self-service window lets you do it yourself.
headings: How far back you can go
Add a session you forgot to clock
articles.body:
What you can fix yourself depends on your organization's employee self-service setting. An admin
can always correct anything.

## How far back you can go

My attendance says which applies to you:

| Self-service         | What you can do yourself                                                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Off                  | Clock in and out and take breaks. Every correction goes through an admin. |
| On, today only       | Enter and correct today, and a session still running from an earlier day. |
| On, a number of days | Enter and correct today and that many days before it.                     |
| On, no limit         | Enter and correct any day of your own employment.                         |

Only organization administrators change this setting, on the Organization page. For a day
outside your window, ask a group admin or an organization admin. After your employment ends, only
an admin can change your attendance.

## Correct a session

1. On My attendance, open the day and press "Correct".
2. Change the clock-in or clock-out time, or a break's times. Add a break with
   "Add break" or remove one.
3. Press "Save correction".

A correction moves times, never days: the start has to stay on the day the session belongs to,
while the end may cross midnight. A session can't end later than now, can't be longer than the
organization's session limit, and can't overlap another session. Breaks stay inside their session
and don't overlap each other.

"History" in the same dialog lists every change to the session, with who made it.

## Add a session you forgot to clock

Press "Add session" on the day, set the start and end, add breaks if you took any, and
save. Switch on "Ends the next day" if it ran past midnight. The session is marked
"Entered" for good, so everyone can tell it wasn't clocked.

An added session must already be over. If you forgot to clock in and are still working, clock in
now and then correct the start time.

## Changes after the day

When you change a session after its day has passed, it shows "Changed after the day", and
your admin sees it flagged on Team attendance until they correct it or mark it as checked.
Nothing is blocked meanwhile.

## Deleting

You can delete a session you entered yourself, or a clocked one from today. A clocked session from
an earlier day can be corrected but only an admin can delete it, and the same goes for a session an
admin entered for you. A deleted session keeps its history and stops counting.

## Admins

Group admins correct and add sessions for the members of their groups, and organization
administrators for everyone, on any day of the person's employment. See
[Team attendance](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/team-attendance/).

While the organization's plan is lapsed, attendance can be read but not corrected.

articles.title: Turn on attendance and set its rules
articles.summary: How an organization admin switches attendance on, and what the timezone, working days, breaks, required time, ceilings, location and self-service settings do.
headings: A different required time for one person
articles.body:
Attendance lets people clock in and out, take breaks and see their worked time. It belongs to the
whole organization, not to one group, and runs on Pro and Enterprise. The owner and organization
administrators set it up on the Organization page, in the
"Attendance" card.

## Turn it on

1. Open Organization and find the "Attendance" card.
2. Choose the "Timezone". It is required, and it sets where one
   day ends: a night shift belongs to the day it started.
3. Switch on "Turn attendance on" and save.

From then on, everyone in the organization sees My attendance in the sidebar, and group
admins and organization administrators also see Team attendance.

## The rules

| Setting                                            | Default                                     | What it does                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Holiday country | none                                        | Public holidays there owe no attendance                               |
| Working days    | Monday-Friday                               | Other days owe nothing; time clocked on them still counts             |
| Break allowance | 30 min                                      | Deducted from every day longer than the threshold, break taken or not |
| Threshold | 6 h                                         | Below it, only breaks actually taken are deducted                     |
| Required per day | 8 h                                         | The worked time each working day asks for                             |
| Balance        | Each day | Show the balance per day or over the month                            |
| Close a session after | 16 h                                        | A session nobody clocked out of closes here and is flagged            |
| Close a break after   | 2 h                                         | A forgotten break ends here and is flagged                            |

[Worked time and your balance](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/worked-time-and-balance/) shows how these add up, and
[Forgotten clock-outs](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/attendance-ceilings/) covers the ceilings.

Required time, breaks, working days and holiday country count for every day, past ones included,
so a change moves earlier balances too. A new timezone applies from the next clock-in. Every change
to these settings is logged with who made it and the values before and after.

## A different required time for one person

For someone whose contract differs, set their own "Required per day" on the
"People" card of the same page. Clear it to return them to the
organization's value. External workers owe no required time.

## Location

"Record location at clock-in and clock-out" is off by default. When on, the browser asks each
person for permission at every clock-in and clock-out. Saying no is never recorded or flagged.
Coordinates are kept for twelve months. Agreeing this with your people is the organization's
responsibility.

## Employee self-service

"Employee self-service" decides whether people may enter sessions they
forgot to clock and correct their own times, and how many days back. It is off for a new
organization. See [Correct your attendance](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/attendance-corrections/).

## When the plan lapses

Attendance goes dormant: nobody can clock in or start a break, but a running session can still be
closed and all history stays readable. Nothing is deleted, and subscribing again restores it.
Switching attendance off works the same way.

articles.title: Add your birthday and share it with your groups
articles.summary: Save your birthday in Settings, choose whether your groups see it and your age, and where shared birthdays appear.
articles.body:
You can add your birthday in Settings. It always shows on your own calendar, and your
groups see it only if you share it.

## Add your birthday

1. Open Settings and find the "Birthday" card.
2. Pick the "Day" and "Month".
3. The "Year" is optional. With a year, everyone who sees your birthday on
   the calendar also sees the age you turn. Leave it empty to keep your age to yourself.
4. Save.

A birthday on 29 February shows on 28 February in other years. Saving works on any plan.

## Share it with your groups

Turn on "Share my birthday with my groups" and save. The switch needs at least one of your groups on a
paid plan: Pro, Enterprise or a custom plan. Without one, the card says so and your birthday stays
on your own calendar.

The "What others see" panel beside the form shows where your birthday appears
right now:

- **Your calendar**: always, with your age if you saved a year.
- **Group calendar**: the groups that see it, once you share.
- **Team calendar feeds**: team calendar feeds include shared birthdays, never with
  your age.
- **Colleagues' Google or Microsoft calendars**: never. Direct sync writes only your own birthday
  into your own calendar.

Turn the switch off, or press "Remove birthday", and your birthday leaves every
group calendar.

## Who sees a shared birthday

Shared birthdays show on the Dashboard calendar with a cake, and in the iPhone app.

- With "Show" set to "Me", you see only your own
  birthday.
- With a group shown, you also see the shared birthdays of that group's members. Showing a group
  needs the View permission.
- Only fellow members see them. An organization administrator who isn't in the group sees none.
- A group whose organization never had a paid plan shows no shared birthdays.

Nobody gets a notification or email about a birthday.

## When the plan ends

If your groups lose their paid plan, a birthday you already share keeps showing there. You can stop
sharing, but turning it back on needs a group on a paid plan again.

## Birthdays in your calendar app

A calendar feed or a direct sync can include birthdays. See
[Subscribe to time off in your calendar app](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/calendar-feed/).

articles.title: Sync your days off straight into Google or Microsoft calendar
articles.summary: How direct sync writes your own approved time off into your Google or Microsoft calendar within seconds, which plan it needs, and how to fix a sync that stopped.
articles.body:
Direct sync writes your own approved time off into your Google or Microsoft calendar within seconds
of a change, with no waiting for a calendar app to reload a feed. It needs a paid plan: at least one
of your groups must belong to an organization on Pro or Enterprise.

## Connect your calendar

1. Open Calendar sync and create a calendar with "Only my records", or use
   one you have. See [Subscribe to time off](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/calendar-feed/).
2. In the "Direct sync" part of its card, press "Connect Google" or "Connect
   Microsoft".
3. Sign in to the provider and allow access to your calendar.

Back in Flexi Day, the card shows "Synced" once the first sync is done.
A calendar syncs to one provider at a time.

Team calendars can't connect. Teammates' days are never written to a personal calendar; use the
subscription link for those.

## What gets written

- Your approved time off, from 12 months back and everything ahead, into your primary calendar.
  That is the calendar your organization's sharing uses to show colleagues when you are away.
- With "Group events" on, the events of every group you are in. With
  "Birthdays" on, only your own birthday.
- Event titles follow the language you use in Flexi Day.

How an absence looks depends on the account:

- **Google Workspace (Business Standard or higher):** a full day shows as a location chip with the
  absence type, a timed absence as Out of office, and Home office sets your working location to Home.
- **Personal Gmail and other Google accounts:** absences show as Busy events. Home office isn't
  synced.
- **Microsoft:** absences show as Out of office. Home office isn't synced.

Flexi Day touches only the events it wrote. Attendance and colleagues' birthdays are never written.

## Sync controls

The connected card shows the "Time zone" used for timed absences; change it
there. The "…" menu beside it holds:

- **"Sync now"** to run a sync at once.
- **"Disconnect"**, which removes every event Flexi Day wrote to that calendar
  and nothing else.

## When it stops

| Card shows                                    | What to do                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Needs reconnecting" | The provider ended access. Press "Reconnect"; events already in your calendar stay. |
| "Paused"         | No paid plan covers you. Nothing is written or removed; syncing resumes once a plan is active.             |
| "Sync failed"         | The last attempt failed. Press "Sync now" to try again.                              |

If Microsoft says an admin must approve Flexi Day, your IT admin approves it once for your company,
and then you connect again.

articles.title: Subscribe to time off in Google, Outlook or Apple Calendar
articles.summary: How to make a calendar feed of your own or your team's time off, add it to your calendar app, and keep its private link safe.
headings: Add it to your calendar app
Why a change doesn't show yet
articles.body:
A calendar feed is a private link your calendar app subscribes to. Add it once and approved time off
keeps appearing in Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar. Feeds are free on every plan. Set
them up on the Calendar sync page.

## Create a calendar

1. Open Calendar sync and press "New calendar".
2. Give it a name.
3. Under "Whose records to include", pick "Only my records" or
   "My team's records". For a team calendar, tick the groups to include.
4. Under "Record types & colors", switch on the leave types you want and pick a colour
   for each. "Group events" and "Birthdays" can go in
   too.
5. Press "Save & get link". The preview beside the form shows what the feed will hold.

You can keep several calendars, for example one for yourself and one per team.

## What a feed holds

- Approved time off only: pending, rejected and cancelled requests stay out.
- The last 12 months and everything ahead.
- On a team calendar, every member of the groups where you see everyone's time off, and only your
  own records in the rest. Colleagues' Sick leave shows as Away, and their notes never go out.
- Birthdays only of people who chose to share them, never with ages.

## Add it to your calendar app

After saving, the page shows "Your private subscription link" and an "Add" button for each app:

- **Google Calendar** opens "Add calendar from URL". The calendar then appears under
  "Other calendars".
- **Outlook / Microsoft 365** opens "Subscribe from web". Name it and press Import.
- **Apple Calendar**: press Add on your Mac or iPhone, confirm, and pick how often it
  refreshes.

To add it later, open the calendar's menu on its card and press "Copy feed URL".

## Why a change doesn't show yet

Your calendar app decides how often it reloads the link, often only once a day, and Flexi Day can't
make it hurry. For last-minute changes, check Flexi Day itself. To get your own days off into Google
or Microsoft within seconds, use [direct sync](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/calendar-direct-sync/) instead.

## Keep the link private

Anyone with the link can see every record in the feed, so treat it like a password. To revoke it,
open the calendar's menu and press "Regenerate token". The old link stops working
at once, and everyone subscribed needs the new one.

"Delete" removes the calendar and stops the feed for good. The card shows when an
app last fetched it.

articles.title: Cancel or change a request
articles.summary: Cancel your own pending or approved time off, and how dates, types and times get changed.
articles.body:
You can cancel your own requests at any time, whether pending or approved. Dates can't be edited:
to move time off, cancel the request and book the new dates.

## Cancel a request

- Open the request from the Dashboard calendar or the Requests page and press
  "Cancel request" in the details. This cancels every day of it.
- Or, on the Requests page, press "Cancel" on the row.

The days are free again straight away and stop counting against your allowance. The request stays
on the Requests page as Cancelled, with who cancelled it. When an approved
request is cancelled, the group's approvers are notified.

## Who else can cancel

The group's approvers, its admins and organization administrators can cancel a member's request too,
with an optional reason saved in its history. The member is notified.

## Change a request

| What you want to change     | How                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dates                       | Cancel and book again. Nobody can edit dates.                                                                    |
| Type, half day, times, note | A group admin, the manager or an organization administrator presses "Edit" in the details. |
| A declined request          | It is final. Book again.                                                                                         |

When someone else edits your request, you get a notice, and its history shows "Updated" with what
changed. A change of type or half day is checked against your allowance again.

## The request history

The details show the request's history to you, the group's approvers and its admins: when it was
requested, approved, declined, cancelled, commented on or edited, and by whom. A change made through
the Assistant or an AI app says so there. Teammates don't see the history.

## Removed from a group

If a group admin removes you from a group, your pending requests there and your approved
time off from tomorrow on are cancelled. Past days and today stay.

articles.title: I can't book time off
articles.summary: Why a time off request is refused or the form won't submit, and what fixes each case.
headings: The range has no working day
"This group is read-only on your current plan."
articles.body:
When Flexi Day refuses a request, the message under the form says why. Find it below.

## "No groups available"

You can book only in a group you belong to. Join one with an invite, or create your own. See
[Join a group with an invite](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/join-a-group/).

## "No access for related group"

You need the Tracked permission to book in a group. Someone who only
oversees a group often has it off. Ask a group admin to turn it on, on the group's
Members tab. See [Group permissions](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/group-permissions/).

## Some days are already booked

You can hold one booking per day, across all your groups. A pending request counts as much as an
approved one. The message lists the days. Cancel or change the request that holds them, or pick other
dates. Days of declined or cancelled requests are free again. See
[Cancel or change a request](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/cancel-or-change-a-request/).

## The range has no working day

Flexi Day skips the days your group doesn't work and its country's public holidays. A range made only
of those, such as a weekend, is refused. Check the group's working days with a group admin.

## It would exceed the allowance

For types with an allowance, such as Vacation, a request can't take
you past the days you have for that year. Your pending requests count too. The
"My balance" card on the Dashboard shows what is left.

- Book fewer days, or a type without an allowance.
- Ask a group admin to raise your allowance for the year. See [Allowances](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/allowances/).

External workers can book only types that draw on no allowance, such as
Non-Paid Leave.

## "This group is read-only on your current plan."

The organization's paid plan ended and this group is over the Free limits, so nobody can book in it
until the owner subscribes again or the group shrinks. See
[When a paid plan ends](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/lapsed-plan/).

## Sick day isn't offered

It shows only where the organization has the Sick day benefit on a paid plan. See
[Offer paid sick days with the Sick day benefit](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/sick-day-benefit/).

## The button stays grey

"Submit Request" waits until the form is complete:

- a group and a type are picked;
- the end date is on or after the start date;
- a note is filled in for Other.

Dates must fall between 1 January this year and 31 December next year.

## Booking for someone else

As a group admin you can book only for members who have Tracked on, and
never for someone who deleted their account. See [Request time off](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/request-time-off/).

articles.title: I can't see someone or their time off
articles.summary: Why a colleague, their time off, their birthday or their attendance is missing from your view, and who can change that.
headings: The person is in another group
A request is missing or looks different
articles.body:
What you see in Flexi Day follows the groups you belong to and the permissions you hold in them.
Find what is missing below.

## The calendar shows only you

- **Show is set to "Me".** Switch it to
  "Group" and pick the group. To open the dashboard that way every time, see
  [Change your settings](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/account-settings/).
- **You don't have the View permission in the group.** Without it you
  see only your own time off there, and the group isn't offered on the dashboard. A group admin can
  turn it on. See [Group permissions](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/group-permissions/).

## The person is in another group

You see the time off of groups you belong to. Someone in another group doesn't appear, even in the
same organization. If your team needs to see them, a group admin can mirror their time off into your
group. See [Show someone's time off from another group](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/mirroring/).

## A request is missing or looks different

- **Declined and cancelled requests** never show to teammates.
- **Sick** shows to teammates as
  "Away". Only the group's approvers and admins see the real type.
- **The leave type filter** may hide it. Check "Filter leave types" on the dashboard.
- **Calendar feeds** carry approved time off only, and your calendar app refreshes them on its own
  schedule. See [Subscribe to time off in your calendar app](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/calendar-feed/).

See [Who sees your time off](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/who-sees-your-time-off/) for the full rules.

## The person left the group

When someone is removed from a group, their pending requests and future bookings there are
cancelled, so those days disappear. Their past days stay.

## A birthday is missing

You see a colleague's birthday only if they chose to share it, you are both members of the group you
are looking at, and the group's organization has had a paid plan. See
[Add your birthday and share it](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/birthdays/).

## Attendance

Team attendance shows only the people you administer, as a group admin or an organization
administrator, and never external workers. Members can't see each other's attendance. See
[See and correct your team's attendance](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/team-attendance/).

## The people directory

The directory is on Enterprise, and the owner turns it on. Which parts of a profile you see depends on
the organization's Permission table: colleagues see the card, photo and work contact by default, not
the job, contact or personal details. See
[Turn on the people directory and decide who sees what](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/people-directory/).

articles.title: Clock in, clock out and take a break
articles.summary: How to clock in and out and take breaks on My attendance, what a session is, and why the clock might be off for you.
headings: Forgot to clock in or out
articles.body:
If your organization uses attendance, you record your working time on My attendance. The
page holds the clock and today's sessions. On a phone browser, the round "Clock" button in
the bottom bar opens the same clock, and the iPhone app has it too.

## Clock in and out

1. Open My attendance.
2. Press "Clock in". The clock shows "Clocked in" and the time since.
3. When you stop, press "Clock out".

Each clock-in to clock-out is one session. You can clock in several times a day; the day adds the
sessions up. The times are the server's, not your device's.

You are clocked in once per organization, however many groups you are in. If you already clocked in
somewhere else, such as on your phone, Flexi Day tells you since when, and you clock out there or
here when you are done.

A session belongs to the day it started, so a night shift that crosses midnight counts on its first
day.

## Take a break

While clocked in, press "Take a break", and "End break" when you are back.
Clocking out ends a running break at the same moment. Breaks count against your worked time; see
[Worked time and your balance](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/worked-time-and-balance/).

## Today's sessions

Under the clock, "Today" lists your sessions and breaks with
"Presence" and "Breaks" totals. Switch to
"Week" or "Month" for earlier days.

## Forgot to clock in or out

- **Forgot to clock out:** a session left running closes by itself at the organization's ceiling, 16
  hours by default, and is flagged. Set the time you really left; see
  [Forgotten clock-outs](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/attendance-ceilings/).
- **Forgot to clock in:** add the session afterwards, if your organization allows it; see
  [Correct your attendance](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/attendance-corrections/).

## Location

Some organizations record where you clock. If yours does, a notice on the clock says so once, and
your browser asks for your location at each clock-in and clock-out. You can say no; the clock
works the same and nothing marks the refusal.

## When the clock is off

- **"Clocking in is off"**: your organization switched attendance off, or its plan lapsed. A
  session you left running can still be closed, and your history stays readable. Ask an org admin.
- **"No attendance for external workers"**: external workers don't clock in and owe no time.
- **"Your employment here has ended, so the clock is closed."**: you have left the organization. Your history stays readable.

You see My attendance in the sidebar only while attendance is on for you, or while you
still have a session running.

articles.title: Create a group for your team
articles.summary: Create a group, set its default allowances, and what a group is for.
headings: Renaming, deleting or leaving a group
articles.body:
A group is the unit Flexi Day tracks time off in, usually a team or an office. Each group has its own
members, approvers, working days, public holidays and allowances. A person can belong to several
groups.

## Create a group

1. Open Groups.
2. In "Create a group", enter the "Group name".
3. Set "Default vacation days" and "Default HO days": the yearly allowances
   new members start with. The form suggests 20 and 60.
4. Press "Create group".

You become the group's manager: you administer it and approve its requests. Your own allowance for
this year opens from the defaults.

## Which organization it belongs to

A new group always goes into your own organization. If you don't have one yet, Flexi Day creates it
on the Free plan and you become its owner. Being an administrator of someone else's organization
doesn't change this: a group you create lands in your own.

## Group limits

Each plan allows a number of groups: 3 on Free, 5 on Pro and 20 on Enterprise, plus any extra group
slots. When they are all used, the form says so. The owner can upgrade or buy a slot on the
Billing page. See [Plans, prices and limits](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/plans-and-limits/).

## Next steps

- Invite your team. See [Invite people to a group](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/invite-people/).
- Set the working days and the public holiday country. See
  [Working days and public holidays](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/group-settings/).
- Give people the right permissions. See [Group permissions](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/group-permissions/).

Each group card on the Groups page shows your role in it and links to its
Members, Quotas, Invites and
Settings tabs.

## Renaming, deleting or leaving a group

The app has no button to rename or delete a group, or to leave one yourself. A group admin can remove a member;
see [Group permissions](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/group-permissions/).

articles.title: Create a Flexi Day account
articles.summary: Sign up with your email or with Google, Microsoft or Apple, and confirm your address.
headings: Sign up with email and password
Sign up with Google, Microsoft or Apple
articles.body:
You create an account on the sign-up page with your name, your work email and a password, or with
Google, Microsoft or Apple. Then you confirm your email address from the email Flexi Day sends you.

If someone invited you to a group, use the link in your invite email instead. It creates your
account and puts you in the group in one step. See [Join a group](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/join-a-group/).

## Sign up with email and password

1. Open the sign-up page and fill in your name, your work email and a password of at least 8
   characters. Type the password twice.
2. Press "Create account".
3. Open the verification email and follow its link. The link is valid for one hour.

Once you confirm, you are signed in and land on the Dashboard. You can't sign in with
your password until the address is confirmed. A password that has appeared in a known data breach is
refused, so pick another one.

## Sign up with Google, Microsoft or Apple

Press "Continue with Google", "Continue with Microsoft" or
"Continue with Apple" on the sign-up page. Flexi Day creates the account with the address
the provider shares and still sends its own email to confirm it. If that address already has a
Flexi Day account, sign in the way you did before and connect the provider from
Settings. See [Sign in to Flexi Day](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/sign-in/).

## The confirmation link expired

Use "Forgot?" on the sign-in page and set a password from the email it sends.
Following that reset link confirms your address too, and you can then sign in. The reset link is
also valid for one hour.

## What happens next

A new account starts in no group, so there is nowhere to book time off yet. The
Dashboard offers two ways forward:

- Join your team's group with the invite link or code you got. See
  [Join a group](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/join-a-group/).
- Create a group of your own. You become its manager, and Flexi Day sets up an organization for you
  on the Free plan. No credit card is needed. See [Create a group](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/create-a-group/).

articles.title: See who is away on the dashboard
articles.summary: Read the dashboard calendar, switch between your own and your group's time off, filter by type, and use the cards beside it.
articles.body:
The Dashboard is the first page after you sign in. Its month calendar shows who is away,
and the cards around it show what needs your attention.

## The calendar

Move between months with the arrows beside the month name. Each request shows on the days it covers,
with the person and the type. A half day carries a "½ day" mark. Public
holidays of the group's country, group events and birthdays show on their days too.

Click a request to open its details. Click an empty day, or drag across days on a computer, to
request time off for those dates. Right-click a day for "Request time off" and,
where your plan has them, "New group event".

## Me or your group

"Show" switches between "Me" and
"Group". With the group, pick which one. You can pick only groups where you
have the View permission; without it you see just your own time off. The group view includes time
off mirrored in from other groups.

To change what the calendar opens with, and to choose between the "Lanes" and
"Stripes" layouts, see [Change your settings](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/account-settings/).

## Filter by type

"Filter leave types" hides or shows types of time off, for example to see only home
office days. The legend under the calendar names the colours.

## The cards

- **Stats:** Pending approvals, Out today,
  Coming up · 14d and Working today.
- **Pending approvals:** for approvers, requests waiting on you, with buttons to decide
  them. Everyone sees their own requests still waiting under
  "Your requests".
- **Out today:** who is off today.
- **My balance:** how many days you have left this year for each type with an
  allowance, across your groups, with pending days noted. See [Allowances](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/allowances/).

## No groups yet

A new account in no group sees "No groups yet" with forms to join a group or create
one. See [Join a group](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/join-a-group/) and [Create a group](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/create-a-group/).

articles.title: Download your data or delete your account
articles.summary: Get a copy of your account data or of what an organization holds about you, and delete your account for good.
articles.body:
Both live at the bottom of Settings: "Your data" for copies of your
data, and "Delete account".

## Download your data

- **Account data.** "Download my account data" saves one JSON file
  at once: your profile, sign-in methods, sessions and devices, settings, notifications, calendar
  connections and birthday. Passwords and tokens are left out.
- **Organization data.** For each organization you work or worked in, you
  can export what it holds about you: employment, groups, quotas, bookings with attachments,
  attendance and the change log. It is prepared in the background as a ZIP, you are notified when it
  is ready, and it stays available for 7 days.

## What deleting your account removes

Deleting removes your sign-in and your personal data for good: your account and its sign-in
methods, your settings, notifications, calendar connections, birthday and AI connections. It can't be
undone.

The organizations you work in keep their records of your leave, attendance and quotas, with their
history, until they end your employment or erase those records.

If you own an organization that has nobody else in it, it is deleted with its groups. Download the
organization export first if you want a copy. Groups you manage in someone else's organization pass
to that organization's owner.

## Delete your account

1. Open Settings and go to "Delete account".
2. Confirm it's you: enter your password, or, if you sign in with Google or Microsoft, sign in again.
3. Read the summary of what goes and what stays, and press "Delete for good".

## When you can't delete yet

The card tells you what is in the way:

- You manage a group in your own organization that still has other members. Remove them first.
- You own an organization where other people still work. Remove them first. Handing an organization
  over to someone else isn't available yet.
- Your organization's subscription will renew. Cancel it in the billing portal first; you give up the
  rest of the paid period. See [Manage your subscription](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/manage-subscription/).

articles.title: Add people without an account and send directory invites
articles.summary: How to add someone to the directory who has no Flexi Day account, and how a directory invite lets them claim that profile as their own.
articles.body:
The directory can hold people who have no Flexi Day account yet, such as a new hire before their
first day or someone who never books leave. A directory invite later lets them take over that
profile with their own account.

## Add a person

1. Open Directory and press "Add person".
2. Enter their name and choose a worker type: "Employee" or
   "External worker".
3. Fill in the card if you like: job title, department, location and who they report to.
4. Add an email if you plan to invite them. It must not belong to anyone else in the organization.
5. Press "Add person". Their profile opens, and you fill in the rest there.

The owner, HR and organization administrators can add people by default, on the Enterprise plan.
The person is marked "No account" for the owner, org admins and HR.

Until they have an account, they are in no group: nobody books leave for them, gives them an
allowance or enters attendance, they get no notifications, and they don't count toward the plan's
member limits.

## Send a directory invite

1. Open their profile. If it has no email yet, add one with "Add email".
2. Press "Send invite".
3. Optionally pick a group under "Also add to a group"; they join it when they accept.
4. Press "Send invite".

The email names the organization and carries the link, valid for 14 days. While it is open the
profile shows "Invite sent". "Send invite again" withdraws the
earlier invite, and so does changing the email on the profile.

## Claiming the profile

Accepting the invite creates their account or signs them in, and the profile becomes theirs. From
then on its name and email follow their account.

- Only an invite links a profile. Someone who signs up with the same email without the invite is
  not linked, and joining the organization another way with that email is refused until the profile
  is claimed or the email changes.
- An ordinary group invite sent to the same address claims the profile too.
- If the person already has an employment in the organization, the claim is refused and an admin
  sorts out the duplicate.
- An invite stops working once the person's employment ends or the profile gets an account.

Turning the directory off withdraws open invites that name no group; invites to a group stay valid.
For inviting people straight into a group, see [Invite people](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/invite-people/).

articles.title: Directory profiles, photos, departments and locations
articles.summary: What each section of a directory profile holds, how to edit your own or someone else's profile and photo, and how departments and locations work.
articles.body:
Each person in the [people directory](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/people-directory/) has a profile, split into six
sections. What you see and can change in each depends on the organization's Permission table.

## The sections

| Section                                        | Holds                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Card         | Name, job title, department, location and who the person reports to                                 |
| Photo        | The profile photo                                                                                   |
| Work contact | Work email and work phone                                                                           |
| Job          | Legal name, employee number, start and leaving dates, probation end, contract type and working time |
| Contact      | Private phone and email, two emergency contacts                                                     |
| Personal     | Home address and date of birth                                                                      |

Contact and Personal are the
sensitive sections: they are encrypted and stay hidden until you press
"Show". See [The read log](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/directory-read-log/).

Probation, contract type, working time and the Personal section
apply to employees only, not to [external workers](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/external-workers/).

## Edit a profile

1. Open the person under Directory, or your own profile.
2. Press "Edit profile".
3. Change the sections marked "Editable" and press
   "Save changes".

Sections you may only read are shown greyed. A few rules:

- The name of someone with an account comes from their account; it can be edited only for a person
  without one.
- Work email is separate from the sign-in email, and colleagues see this one.
- Phones are one number in international form, with no extension.
- Reports to is informational and grants nothing.
- The leaving date is informational too: it ends nothing.
- The employee number must be unique among current staff.
- An emergency contact needs both a name and a phone.

"Profile history" lists who changed which fields and when, never the values. The
owner, organization administrators and HR can open it.

## Profile photo

On the edit page, press "Upload photo" and pick a PNG, JPEG, WebP or HEIC
image of at most 10 MB. It saves at once. The photo shows on directory pages only; the calendar,
reports and attendance keep the account picture. Location data is stripped, and photos are never
used for face recognition. By default you, HR and org admins can change it.

## Departments and locations

Each organization keeps its own lists, under "Departments and locations" in
Directory settings. A person holds at most one of each. They aren't tied to groups, and a
location's country only sets where its people's phone numbers start.

An entry someone holds can't be deleted; archive it instead. An archived entry leaves the pickers,
and people who hold it keep it, shown as "(archived)". The owner, HR and org admins manage the lists
by default.

## On a lapsed plan

Without Enterprise the directory stays readable, and values can be cleared but not set.

articles.title: Sensitive sections and the read log
articles.summary: Why Contact and Personal stay hidden until you press Show, what the read log records about who opened them, and who can read the log.
headings: When someone asks what you hold
articles.body:
Contact (private phone, private email, emergency contacts) and Personal (home address, date of birth)
are the sensitive sections of a [directory profile](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/directory-profiles/). They are stored
encrypted, and nobody sees their values by just opening a profile.

## Open a sensitive section

On a profile, the section reads "Hidden until you open it.". Press
"Show" to see it. You can only do this where the Permission table lets you
read the section: by default the person themselves, HR, organization administrators and the owner.

Opening someone else's section is recorded in the read log, and the page says so. Opening your own
profile records nothing. Once opened, the section stays open while you stay on that person's
profile and its edit page.

## What the read log records

Each entry has who opened it, whose profile, which section, when, and the audience that allowed it,
such as HR or Org admin. It never holds the values. Exports of a person's data are logged there
too. A section opened through an AI app or the Assistant shows "through an AI app" or
"through the Assistant" under the reader.

Entries are kept for 12 months and then removed. They stay even after the person is erased, as
they hold no values.

## Read the log

The owner and organization administrators open "Read log" in
Directory settings on the Directory page. Filter it by person or by reader, and
press "Show older" to go further back. HR can't read the log, and
the iPhone app never shows it.

While the directory is off, the owner and org admins still reach the log from the
"People directory" card on the Organization page.

## When someone asks what you hold

If a person asks who accessed their data, the read log answers it. A copy of everything their
profile holds comes from the person export, which the owner and organization administrators run
from the profile. It also lists the read log entries about them, with a purpose such as HR
administration in place of the readers' names.

articles.title: Emails from Flexi Day don't arrive
articles.summary: What to check when a confirmation, password reset, sign-in code, invite or request email doesn't reach you.
articles.body:
Flexi Day sends its emails from an address at flexi-day.com. If one doesn't arrive, work through the
steps for the kind of email you expected.

## First checks

- **Spam and junk.** Look there and in any "Promotions" or "Other" tab. Mark the email as not spam so
  the next one lands in your inbox.
- **The right address.** Emails go to the address you signed up with. The user menu in the top bar
  shows it. For an invite, check the address with whoever invited you.
- **Company mail filters.** Some work mailboxes hold or drop mail from new senders. Ask your IT team
  to allow mail from flexi-day.com.

## Confirming your email address

The confirmation link is valid for one hour. If it expired or never came, use
"Forgot?" on the sign-in page and set a password from the email it sends.
Following that link confirms your address too. See
[Create a Flexi Day account](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/create-an-account/).

## Password reset and sign-in codes

- A password reset link is valid for one hour. Ask for a new one if it expired.
- A two-factor code sent by email is valid for 3 minutes. Press "Resend code" on
  the sign-in screen for a fresh one, or use your authenticator app or a backup code instead. See
  [Sign in to Flexi Day](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/sign-in/).

## Group invites

An invite works only for the address it was sent to and expires after 14 days. If it doesn't arrive,
ask a group admin to copy the invite code from the group's Invites tab and
send it to you another way. Enter it in "Join a group" on the Groups page. See
[Join a group with an invite](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/join-a-group/).

## Emails about requests

- **The setting is off.** "Email notifications" in Settings turns off
  emails about requests: approval requests, decisions, cancellations and comments. The notices still
  show under the bell in the top bar.
- **Some notices never email.** A request an admin filed or changed for you, an auto-closed clock and
  a ready export show only in the app. See [Notifications and emails](https://www.flexi-day.com/help/notifications/) for the
  full list.
- **You didn't need one.** You get no email about your own actions, and approvers aren't told about a
  request they filed themselves.

## Still nothing

If none of this helps, write to us through the Contact page linked at the bottom of
flexi-day.com. Name your address and the email you expected.

articles.title: End someone's employment, and when they come back
articles.summary: How an employment starts and ends with and without the directory, what End employment changes, where people who left are listed, and how a returning person's new spell can copy from the old one.
articles.body:
An employment is one person's time working for one organization. It starts when they first join one
of its groups or are added to the directory, and it carries their attendance and directory profile.
One stretch from start to end is called a spell.

## How an employment ends

- **Without the directory:** it ends by itself when the person loses their last link to the
  organization, such as being removed from their last group. The owner and organization
  administrators can also end it from the "People" card on the
  Organization page.
- **With the directory on:** removing someone from a group never ends their employment. They stay
  employed, in no group, until someone ends it by hand. The owner and org admins find them with the
  "No group" filter on the directory page.

## End employment

1. Open the person's profile under Directory.
